description:
TerraAnalog — Exploring Earth to Understand Other Worlds

TerraAnalog is an AI-powered platform that identifies Earth locations with environmental and terrain characteristics similar to the Moon and Mars.

By combining IoT sensor measurements, GPS coordinates, site images, geospatial analysis, and open NASA data, TerraAnalog helps discover potential terrestrial analog environments for future space missions.
summary:
NAZEER is an integrated planetary-analogue exploration platform designed to identify and evaluate Earth locations that resemble selected environments on Mars and the Moon. It combines two complementary approaches: an ESP32-powered mobile rover that measures temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, surface tilt, and altitude, and a web-based dashboard that collects and analyzes environmental data for selected locations, including daily climate data from NASA POWER.

Users can select and document terrestrial sites, visualize their locations on an interactive map, compare multiple candidates, and evaluate them against planetary reference profiles such as Gale Crater, Jezero Crater, and the lunar Shackleton region. NAZEER applies an experimental weighted comparison model to generate a similarity score, display individual environmental factors, and produce analytical reports.

By connecting real-world field measurements with open environmental data and planetary reference conditions, NAZEER helps researchers and exploration teams investigate potential Earth analog sites for testing rover technologies and supporting future lunar and Martian missions. The platform also highlights the limitations of Earth analogues, including differences in gravity, atmospheric conditions, and space radiation.
details:
NAZEER – Project Details

1. What does your project do, and how does it work?

NAZEER is an integrated planetary-analogue exploration system that combines a physical environmental rover with a scientific web-based analysis platform to investigate how closely selected locations on Earth resemble environments on Mars and the Moon.

The project works through two complementary components:

A. Smart Environmental Rover

We developed a mobile, four-wheel rover powered by an ESP32 microcontroller and equipped with environmental sensors. It measures:

  • Air temperature.
  • Relative humidity.
  • Atmospheric pressure.
  • Surface inclination (tilt).
  • Altitude above sea level.

The rover transmits its measurements to the web dashboard through wireless MQTT communication, with a direct USB Serial connection also supported for hardware monitoring. The dashboard displays incoming measurements and their history, allowing users to observe real-world environmental conditions.

B. Planetary Analysis Dashboard

The web platform allows users to select Earth locations, retrieve environmental data, explore candidate sites on interactive maps, and compare their characteristics with selected Martian and lunar reference locations.

It retrieves daily climate data from the NASA POWER API, including temperature, relative humidity, and surface pressure. The platform also uses additional environmental services, such as Open-Meteo, for elevation and supporting environmental indicators. Planetary reference profiles and linked NASA mission resources provide context for the Mars and Moon comparisons.

A weighted comparison model evaluates environmental and terrain characteristics, generates an overall similarity score, and presents individual factor scores and data-coverage information. Users can also compare multiple candidate locations and generate analytical reports.

2. What benefits does it have?

NAZEER provides several benefits:

  • Practical Field Testing: The rover enables real-world environmental measurements instead of relying exclusively on pre-existing datasets.
  • Data-Driven Site Evaluation: It helps users identify and compare Earth locations that share selected environmental and terrain characteristics with extraterrestrial environments.
  • Integrated Exploration: It brings rover telemetry, remote environmental datasets, planetary references, interactive maps, and scientific visualizations into one platform.
  • Transparent Comparisons: Users can examine the contribution of individual factors instead of relying only on a single similarity percentage.
  • Educational Value: It makes planetary science, environmental data analysis, IoT, and rover technologies more accessible through practical exploration.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our intended impact is to support the preparation and testing of future planetary exploration technologies by helping researchers, students, and exploration teams investigate suitable terrestrial analogue environments.

Earth-based analogue locations can provide valuable environments for testing rover mobility, environmental sensors, data collection workflows, and field-operation procedures before conducting similar activities on the Moon or Mars.

NAZEER also aims to encourage interdisciplinary collaboration between planetary science, environmental analysis, robotics, and software engineering.

Importantly, an Earth analogue cannot fully reproduce extraterrestrial conditions. Differences in gravity, atmospheric composition, radiation, and extreme environmental conditions must still be considered when interpreting the results.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Hardware and Electronics

  • ESP32 microcontroller.
  • Four-wheel mobile rover platform.
  • Environmental sensors for temperature, humidity, and atmospheric pressure.
  • Tilt / inclination measurement sensor.
  • Altitude measurement capability.

Programming Languages

  • HTML – Dashboard structure.
  • CSS – Interface styling and responsive layouts.
  • JavaScript – API integration, data processing, calculations, and interactivity.
  • C/C++ – ESP32 firmware and hardware control.
  • Esp code: Nasa Code

APIs and Data Sources

  • NASA POWER API – Earth climate and environmental data.
  • Open-Meteo Elevation API – Terrain elevation data.
  • Open-Meteo Forecast and Air Quality APIs – Supporting environmental indicators.
  • Wikimedia REST API – Geographic and location-related descriptive information.
  • NASA Mars and Moon mission resources – Planetary reference information, including Mars Trek, MOLA, Moon Trek, LOLA, CRISM, M³, and LCROSS.

Libraries and Software Technologies

  • Tailwind CSS – Responsive interface development.
  • Three.js – Three-dimensional planetary visualization.
  • Leaflet.js – Interactive maps.
  • Chart.js – Environmental data visualization.
  • Lucide – Interface icons.
  • MQTT.js and HiveMQ Public MQTT Broker – Rover-to-dashboard communication.
  • Web Serial API – Direct USB communication with the ESP32.
  • Esri ArcGIS World Topographic Map – Map visualization.

5. How is your project creative?

NAZEER's main innovation is the combination of a physical environmental rover and a planetary comparison platform in a single workflow.

Instead of treating planetary analogue research as a static data comparison, NAZEER connects real-world field measurements with remote environmental datasets and planetary reference conditions.

Its creative aspects include:

  • A dual approach combining physical sensor measurements and remote data retrieval.
  • A planetary comparison engine that uses different evaluation weights for Mars and the Moon, reflecting their different environmental conditions.
  • A factor-by-factor similarity breakdown that explains how temperature, pressure, humidity, slope, and geological characteristics contribute to the result.
  • Dynamic handling of unavailable measurements, preventing missing data from being incorrectly treated as zero.
  • Interactive planetary visualizations, location exploration, and multi-site comparisons.
  • An exploratory In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) readiness indicator to introduce resource-related considerations into site analysis.

This combination transforms environmental data into an interactive exploration and decision-support experience.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered several environmental, geological, technical, and scientific factors when designing the platform and its comparison model.

Environmental Factors

  • Temperature similarity.
  • Atmospheric pressure.
  • Relative humidity.
  • Elevation and altitude.
  • Environmental data availability and coverage.

Terrain and Geological Factors

  • Surface inclination and slope.
  • Terrain characteristics and geological features.
  • Similarities in surface materials and landforms.
  • Potential relevance of features such as basalt, regolith, craters, dunes, and ice-related environments.

Planet-Specific Differences

We designed different comparison configurations for Mars and the Moon because their environments are fundamentally different.

For Mars, the experimental model assigns nominal weights of:

  • Terrain: 40%.
  • Temperature: 25%.
  • Atmospheric pressure: 20%.
  • Relative humidity: 15%.

For the Moon, the experimental model assigns:

  • Terrain: 65%.
  • Temperature: 35%.

Atmospheric pressure and humidity are excluded from the lunar similarity calculation because the Moon has no substantial atmosphere. Their weights are therefore not treated as meaningful lunar comparison factors.

Data Quality and Scientific Limitations

We also considered:

  • Missing or invalid measurements.
  • Differences in data sources, measurement methods, and temporal coverage.
  • The need to distinguish measured rover readings from simulated or test data.
  • The importance of reporting data coverage before presenting a similarity score.
  • The limitations of terrestrial analogues, particularly differences in gravity, atmospheric composition, radiation, and thermal conditions.

The similarity model uses project-defined experimental weights and scoring functions. It is intended as an exploratory comparison tool, not as a formally validated planetary-site certification system.
